newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie freed from jail on parole.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie freed from jail on parole.

text.p: Bankrupt French tycoon and soccer boss Bernard Tapie was freed on parole on Friday after serving almost six months in prison for rigging a soccer match.
The former cabinet minister and chairman of Marseille soccer club left the Luynes jail in southern France after an appeal court in nearby Aix-en-Provence accepted his request for parole.
Tapie, sentenced to eight months in jail for rigging a 1993 league match between Marseille and Valenciennes, had been in prison since February 3.
The bribes secured Marseille an easy victory days before Tapie's team played the 1993 European Cup final against AC Milan. Marseille won the final 1-0.
Tapie's plans were unknown but an acquaintance said he might stay with a friend near Marseille. Under parole restrictions, Tapie will have to stay in France.

The 54-year-old Tapie, who faces a barrage of lawsuits over his collapsed business empire, is currently appealing against an 18-month sentence imposed by a court on July 4 for embezzling funds from the Marseille soccer club.
He was found guilty of embezzling 100 million francs ($16.13 million) between 1987 and 1993.
